title.narrative: Regulatory Impact Assessment of new ambient air quality pollutant limits

description.narrative: The UAE’s outdoor air quality is currently regulated by the 2006 Decree No. 12 Regulation Concerning Protection of Air from Pollution. This decree covers seven key air pollutants which are: Sulphur dioxide (SO2), Carbon monoxide (CO), Nitrogen dioxide (NO2), Total suspended particles (TSP), Particulate matter less than 10 microns in diameter (PM10), Lead (Pb) and Ozone (O3). These regulations do not include particulate matter less than 2.5 microns in diameter (PM2.5). Long term exposure to PM2.5 has been documented to have much more detrimental risks to health as it can penetrate deep into the lungs and even enter the bloodstream, leading to serious health problems. PM2.5 has been associated with a higher burden of disease including but not limited to ischemic heart disease, lung cancer, pulmonary obstruction, stroke and adverse birth outcomes. The 2019 air quality inventory of the UAE mapped the key sectors that are responsible for PM2.5 pollutant emissions and the leading sector that was identified was the mining operations of non-metallic minerals (i.e. clinker and lime production, cement). The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) is leading efforts to reduce the emission of PM2.5 in the country and has embarked on a process of assessing multiple options to curb PM2.5 emissions. While the health impact of PM2.5 is significant, the UAE is also considering the revision to update the limits of the other pollutants covered by Decree no. 12 of 2006, where new pollutant limits have been proposed. This project will involve undertaking a detailed regulatory impact assessment of the proposed PM2.5 limit, and the new limits of the other ambient air pollutants, considering the costs and benefits to the economy, health and wellbeing.
